    <h1 class="bok-title">The ML Systems Taxonomy</h1>
    <p class="bok-lede">A shared map of what an ML systems engineer needs to know. We built this taxonomy to structure the four-volume <em>Machine Learning Systems</em> textbook series—connecting chapters, labs, simulators, and StaffML questions across the <strong>lifecycle</strong> that builds a system, the <strong>stack</strong> it runs on, the <strong>qualities</strong> it is judged by, and shared <strong>foundations</strong>—and we are sharing it openly in case a common vocabulary is helpful to the broader field. Each subject has a code you can cite, and each concept has a page showing what it affects and where the books teach it. Spot a missing concept, a misplaced subject, or a relationship to refine? <a href="https://github.com/harvard-edge/cs249r_book/issues/new?template=taxonomy_feedback.yml">Suggest an addition or correction on GitHub &rarr;</a></p>

  <details class="bok-about">
    <summary>About this taxonomy: scope, method, tagging, and known gaps</summary>
    <p><strong>How it is built.</strong> This taxonomy adopts published standards: <a href="https://groups.niso.org/higherlogic/ws/public/download/6484/Guidelines%20for%20the%20Construction,%20Format,%20and%20Management%20of%20Monolingual%20Controlled%20Vocabularies.pdf">ANSI/NISO Z39.19</a> for construction and <a href="https://www.w3.org/TR/skos-reference/">W3C SKOS</a> for representation. The <a href="https://github.com/harvard-edge/cs249r_book/blob/dev/taxonomy/METHOD.md">method statement</a> marks each recommendation met, partial, or open.</p>
    <div class="bok-about-body">
      <p>We developed this taxonomy as the structural backbone for the four-volume <em>Machine Learning Systems</em> textbook series and share it openly so educators, researchers, and engineering teams can reuse or adapt it. No published, community-endorsed body of knowledge for ML systems existed when this draft was written: courses split between a compute-stack tradition (deep learning systems) and a production tradition (ML systems design and MLOps). This taxonomy joins the two and adds what both tend to leave out: datacenter infrastructure, safety and assurance, sustainability, and agentic and embodied systems.</p>
      <p>Each concept has one home, the subject that owns its mechanism; other placements appear as related subjects. The taxonomy organizes knowledge for browsing and does not prescribe a course order or prerequisites. Relationships are editorial drafts, each with the condition under which it holds. Book links point to where MLSysBook teaches a subject; a missing link is unfinished alignment, not evidence that the books omit it.</p>
      <p>This is an editorial draft for expert review, not a claim of completeness, consensus, or demonstrated learning. Community suggestions and corrections are welcome via the <a href="https://github.com/harvard-edge/cs249r_book/issues/new?template=taxonomy_feedback.yml">GitHub taxonomy feedback form</a>.</p>
      <div class="bok-known-gaps" id="bok-tagging"></div>
      <div class="bok-known-gaps" id="bok-gaps"></div>
      <p class="bok-method" id="bok-method"></p>
    </div>
  </details>
